label: sec:bach-intro-prose
html:
Richard Feynman described electron diffraction as a phenomenon "which has in it the heart of quantum mechanics. In reality, it contains the only mystery" [feynman1965]. He went on to describe a thought experiment for which he stated "that you should not try to set up" because "the apparatus would have to be made on an impossibly small scale to show the effects we are interested in."

Bach et al. [bach2013] demonstrate the full realization of this thought experiment. They report both control over individual slits to observe probability distributions P_1, P_2, and P_{12} from single- and double-slits, and the build-up of a diffraction pattern at single-electron detection rates.

The general perception that the electron double-slit experiment has already been performed is true only in the sense that Jönsson (1961) demonstrated diffraction from multiple micro-slits without single particle detection, and Tonomura (1989) recorded single-electron buildup using biprisms rather than true double-slits. This paper is the first to combine both elements: true nano-fabricated double-slits with single-electron event recording.
